clue.text: Revellers sing, interrupting book experts

indicators.note: one word breaking into another means it goes inside it

parts.note: aces are experts, top performers
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: Singers drown out a gathering of literary specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' splits the experts' word in two; 'book' stands first though the surface puts it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchantes were the frenzied female followers of Bacchus, so the word now means wild revellers.

clue.text: Bill about to dispose of new attire

indicators.note: disposing of something gets rid of it, so the letter for new is dropped from the bill

parts.note: an account is a bill to be paid
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone sorting out paperwork is about to throw out a new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as one phrase but splits: 'about' is RE, 'to dispose of' the deletion indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre is to dress or equip someone, a formal verb for clothing them.

clue.text: One engraves daily touring Home Counties

indicators.note: a tourist goes round a place, so the cleaner's word goes round the region's letters

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning lady who comes in daily
SE, the south-east of England, is where the Home Counties lie

explanation.surface: An everyday cleaner travels round the counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaning lady; the Home Counties surround London, in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing is decorating metal by engraving or embossing, so a chaser is a craftsman who does it.

clue.text: Nearly all key marginals sponge?

indicators.note: nearly the whole word means it stops one letter short of its end
the margins of a word are its outside letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: Almost every important seat in an election might soak things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts ALL to AL; 'marginals' takes the outside letters of 'key', KY. In Britain marginals are seats that could change hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is slang for a heavy drinker who soaks up alcohol, as is alky; the question mark flags the slang.

clue.text: Like lab work if it's nice and constant

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A cheerful view of laboratory work: pleasant and reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges IFITSNICE into SCIENTIFI; C ends it. 'lab work' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'lab'.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is the home of experiment, so anything lab-like is scientific in character.

clue.text: Hamper holding tin booze container

indicators.note: one word holding another keeps it inside

parts.note: to hamper is to hinder or deter
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A picnic basket containing a tin of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' reads as a basket but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel that wine or spirits are poured into for serving.

clue.text: Take in this writer's good book lecturer left out

parts.note: the setter's 'this writer is' becomes I'M

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so the letter goes from the word

parts.note: the Good Book is the Bible

explanation.surface: An author absorbs a worthwhile book, minus the professor's input.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not the usual L here; it belongs with 'out' as the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink or absorb, taking something into oneself.

clue.text: Clever clogs ignoring one product of grinder

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so the letter for one drops away

parts.note: a clever clogs is a brain, a know-all
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A know-all brushing off someone, something to do with milling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes I from BRAIN. Clever clogs is British slang for a smart person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk separated from grain when it is ground in a mill.

clue.text: Lush salmon fills everyone in charge

indicators.note: one thing filling another sits inside it

parts.note: all means everyone
the coho is a Pacific salmon

explanation.surface: A rich salmon dish feeds everybody, with someone in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' reads as an adjective but is a noun for a drunk; the coho is a Pacific salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is slang for a habitual heavy drinker, which is what an alcoholic is.

clue.text: Westbound soldiers eating first of milled cereal

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, an army corps

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Troops heading west consume some freshly ground grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westbound' turns REME into EMER; 'eating' puts the M from 'first of milled' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmer is an ancient variety of wheat, a grain crop still grown in places.

clue.text: Linguist's writing in prison

definitions.note: read as 'Linguist is', so it names the man

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: choky is British slang for prison
MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A language scholar's work written behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Choky is old British slang for jail, from Hindi.
explanation.definitionFit: Noam Chomsky is the American scholar whose theories of grammar reshaped linguistics.

clue.text: Delight aunt, say, losing head

indicators.note: losing the head of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: an aunt is an example of a relation

explanation.surface: Please an aunt, perhaps, then she has her head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes R off RELATION. 'say' signals that the aunt is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness, a feeling of joy or delight.

clue.text: Dessert's briefly succeeding

indicators.note: a brief version of a word is cut short at its end

parts.note: read as 'Dessert is'; afters is British slang for dessert

explanation.surface: A pudding is next up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the final S off AFTERS, the British word for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: After means following on from, so something after another is succeeding it.

clue.text: Shredded hot spuds retaining temperature

parts.note: in means fashionable, hot right now

indicators.note: keeping something retained inside it

parts.note: taters is slang for potatoes, as is spuds

explanation.surface: Shredded hot potatoes stay warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' means trendy rather than warm; taters is British slang for potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in tatters is torn into rags and strips.

clue.text: Always wanting more banalities to be broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A greedy appetite for dull remarks on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be broadcast' rearranges the letters of 'banalities'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiable means impossible to satisfy, never content with what one has.

clue.text: Smooth small people carrier conserves energy

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it, holding it inside

parts.note: a tramline carries trams full of people
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A compact family car is fuel-efficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conserves' puts E inside TRAMLINE after S. A people carrier is a British term for a minivan, but here it is a tramline.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline is to smooth the shape of something, or simplify a process.

clue.text: Drunken row was therefore brewing

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture stewed together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A boozy argument was therefore building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges 'row was therefore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone the worse for wear is in poor shape, especially from too much alcohol.

clue.text: Working guy owing money, pending trial?

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: owing money is being in the red, so 'owing' puts the guy in the red

parts.note: money owed is shown in red ink, hence RED for the debt
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A man in a job is in debt and awaiting court.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in the red' (in debt) supplies both the container RED and the sense of inside that 'owing' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant on remand is held in custody or on bail until the trial comes to court.

clue.text: Finally wipe gold tool without using cold spirit

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: doing without something leaves it out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a device is a tool
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Cleaning up gold with an implement and no chilled liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' gives E from wipe; 'without using' removes the C from DEVICE, leaving DEVIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie is French brandy, a clear spirit distilled from fruit.

clue.text: Town's bowled over about pub, one that's decadent

indicators.note: one word about another goes round it
knocked over, so the word is turned upside down, in a down-style reading back to front

parts.note: a city is a town, with the 's kept as S
a bar is a pub
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A town is astonished by a bar that turns out to be a den of excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' turns the town's word round to SYTIC, which 'about' then wraps round the pub and the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaris was an ancient Greek city famed for luxury, so sybaritic means self-indulgent.

clue.text: British tree showing less growth on crown

parts.note: the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A British tree has a thinner canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown' is the top of a tree in the surface but the top of a head in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone balder has less hair on top of the head.

clue.text: Tanks, an issue of pride in South Africa

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a cub is the offspring, the issue, of a pride of lions

explanation.surface: Military vehicles are a matter of national pride for South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' is a group of lions, and 'issue' its young.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba gear is chiefly the air tanks a diver carries, so tanks stand for it.

clue.text: Stewed pears at duke's banquet

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Poached pears are served at a nobleman's feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stewed' rearranges 'pears' to SPREA; D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is an informal word for a lavish meal laid out on the table.

clue.text: Cover over novel puzzle

indicators.note: turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: Wrapping up a new conundrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as new but names Jane Austen's book.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a quandary, a problem with no clear answer.

clue.text: Ruin lawyer's husband

parts.note: a DA, district attorney, is a lawyer; with the 's that gives DAS

explanation.surface: A lawyer wrecks her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is a US district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash hopes is to ruin or destroy them.

clue.text: Fish swallows line and weight

indicators.note: something swallowed goes inside

parts.note: the barbel is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish takes the hook, line and sinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts L into BARBEL, beside its own L.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbell is a bar with weights on both ends, lifted in the gym.

clue.text: Contents of 24? Bar's missing litres

indicators.note: missing something means it is left out

parts.note: read as 'Bar is'; to bar is to block

explanation.surface: A beer mug's contents; the pub is short of measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops L from BLOCK. 24 is STEIN, a German beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Bock is a strong German beer, the sort of drink a stein holds.

clue.text: Mug genius snubbing a German

indicators.note: snubbing someone cuts them out, so the letters are removed

parts.note: Einstein is the byword for a genius
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A fool of a genius ignores a man from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbing' removes EIN from the front of EINSTEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware beer mug of German style.

clue.text: Personal drink delivery left reserves in case

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a legal case is an action
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's army reserve

explanation.surface: A personal courier drops off a drink, leaving supplies in a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve force; a case is a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactation is a mother producing milk for her baby, a drink delivered in person.
